output.population: Adults with type 2 diabetes in meta-analyses of randomized weight-loss diet trials and intervention studies reporting diabetes remission.
output.intervention: Weight-loss approaches including very-low-energy diets, formula meal replacement, low-carbohydrate, high-protein, Mediterranean, high-MUFA, vegetarian, low-GI and other diets.
output.intervention_or_exposure: Weight-loss dietary approaches for people with type 2 diabetes.
output.comparator: Various control or comparator diets across included reviews and trials.
output.outcome: Weight loss and type 2 diabetes remission, largely within 1 year.
output.effect: Very-low-energy diets (400-500 kcal/day for 8-12 weeks) achieved 6.6 kg greater weight loss than low-energy diets (95% CI -9.5 to -3.7; GRADE low). Formula meal replacements achieved 2.4 kg greater weight loss over 12-52 weeks (95% CI -3.3 to -1.4; GRADE moderate). Low-carbohydrate diets were no better for weight loss than higher-carbohydrate/low-fat diets (GRADE high). For remission at 1 year, RCTs with initial low-energy total diet replacement reported a median 54% remission; evidence for ketogenic/very-low-carbohydrate and very-low-energy food-based diets was very low certainty.
output.applicability_boundary: Applies to adults with type 2 diabetes and mainly short-term evidence of 1 year or less; long-term effects on weight, glycemic control, clinical outcomes, and complications remain uncertain.
output.source_span: Very low energy diets and formula meal replacement appear the most effective approaches, generally providing less energy than self-administered food-based diets.

uncertainties: Most evidence was restricted to 1 year or less.
Quality and certainty varied substantially across diet types and reviews.
